skill.name: wap-ingestion
skill.description: Guides safe Bauplan data ingestion from S3 with the Write-Audit-Publish pattern, temporary branches, quality checks, and controlled publishing.
skill.summary: Guide S3 data ingestion into Bauplan with a branch-based Write-Audit-Publish workflow.
skill.author: BauplanLabs

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around prose, SDK method names, and code fences. The skill does include legitimate local command usage for running the generated WAP script and for Bauplan CLI merge or cleanup steps, so those command-oriented findings are confirmed as medium risk. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration intent, or malicious network behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Show the generated script path and command arguments, then require explicit user confirmation before running it.

remediation.issue: CLI merge and branch deletion steps
remediation.suggestion: Keep inspect as the default and require a separate confirmation before merging to main or deleting a branch.
Add dataset-specific checks such as schema, null rate, duplicate key, and expected row range checks before publish.

content.value_statement: Data teams need a safer way to load S3 files into Bauplan without changing main immediately. This skill guides a branch-based Write-Audit-Publish flow with checks before publish.
actual_capabilities: Collects the S3 path, target table name, and branch handling choices before script creation.
Guides a Python SDK workflow that creates a temporary branch from main.
Supports creating new tables from S3 files and appending data to existing tables.
Adds an audit phase that verifies imported row counts before publishing.
Explains inspect, merge, keep, and delete outcomes for success and failure paths.
Provides manual CLI merge steps after a user reviews the temporary branch.
limitations: Requires Bauplan credentials, access to the source S3 location, and the Bauplan Python SDK.
The default audit only checks that at least one row was imported.
The template expects users to customize table names, namespaces, and source paths correctly.
Manual merge steps require the Bauplan CLI and a correctly selected branch.

use_cases.title: Load a New S3 Dataset
use_cases.description: Create a temporary Bauplan branch, ingest S3 files, and inspect row counts before publication.

use_cases.title: Append to an Existing Table
use_cases.description: Use the existing table path to import new S3 rows while keeping changes isolated on a branch.

use_cases.title: Review a Controlled Publish
use_cases.description: Keep the branch open after ingestion so a reviewer can inspect data before merging to main.

prompt_templates.scenario: Keep the branch open for manual review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a WAP ingestion script for my S3 dataset. Use inspect on success and keep the branch on failure.

prompt_templates.scenario: Add data to an existing table and extend the audit.

prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced branch workflow for related tables.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a WAP ingestion workflow for multiple related Bauplan tables. Keep all changes on one branch and explain the publish decision points.

output_examples.input: A user wants to append new files to an existing table.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains how to skip table creation, import data on a branch, and validate the appended rows before merge.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks how to publish an inspected branch.
output_examples.output: The assistant describes the required main checkout, merge action, and optional branch cleanup with confirmation points.

best_practices: Keep the default inspect behavior until a human has reviewed the imported data.
Add dataset-specific quality checks before allowing a merge to main.
Use clear table names and branch names so reviewers can trace the ingestion source.
anti_patterns: Do not merge to main before validating row counts and expected schema behavior.
Do not delete failed branches when they are needed for debugging or audit evidence.
Do not reuse the template without replacing example S3 paths and table names.

faq.question: What does WAP mean in this skill?
faq.answer: WAP means Write-Audit-Publish. The data is written to a branch, checked, and then published only after review.

faq.question: Does this skill publish data to main automatically?
faq.answer: The default behavior keeps the branch open for inspection. Automatic merge is only used when the user selects that behavior.

faq.question: What file sources are covered?
faq.answer: The instructions focus on S3 URI patterns for formats such as parquet, CSV, and JSONL files.

faq.question: Can I use this for an existing table?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains an append path that skips table creation and imports data into an existing table on a branch.

faq.question: What audit checks are included?
faq.answer: The template verifies that imported row count is greater than zero. Users should add checks for their data contract.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
